questions.question: The HCF of 28 p⁵q² and 70 p³q⁴ is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **HCF** of numerical coefficients: **HCF(28, 70) = 14**.

For variables, take the **lowest power** of each common base.

Lowest power of **p** is **p³** and lowest power of **q** is **q²**.

Combine them: **14 × p³ × q²**.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 p³q².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First term = **28 p⁵q²**, Second term = **70 p³q⁴**.

**Formula:** **HCF** = Product of the **common prime factors** with the **smallest power**.

⇒ Prime factorization of 28 = 2² × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 70 = 2 × 5 × 7

⇒ **HCF of (28, 70)** = 2¹ × 7¹ = 14

⇒ Common variables are **p** and **q**.

⇒ Smallest power of **p** in both terms = **p³**

⇒ Smallest power of **q** in both terms = **q²**

⇒ **Total HCF** = 14 × p³ × q² = 14 p³q²

**∴ The correct answer is 14 p³q².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM of Monomials

To find the **LCM**, take the **highest power** of each variable and the **LCM** of the coefficients.

HCF of Fractions

**HCF** = HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators.

Product Rule

For any two numbers, **Product of numbers = HCF × LCM**.</p

questions.question: If the ratio of the sine of an acute angle to its cosine is 5 : 12, then what will the value of sine of that angle be?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The given ratio **sin θ : cos θ = 5 : 12** implies **tan θ = 5/12**.

Using the standard **Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13)**, where Perpendicular = 5 and Base = 12.

The **Hypotenuse** must be 13.

Since **sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse**, the value is 5/13.

**∴ The correct answer is 5/13.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of **sin θ** to **cos θ** is 5 : 12.

**Formula:** **tan θ = sin θ / cos θ** and **sin θ = P / H**.

⇒ sin θ / cos θ = 5 / 12

⇒ tan θ = 5 / 12

⇒ Let Perpendicular (P) = 5k and Base (B) = 12k

⇒ Hypotenuse (H) = √(P² + B²)

⇒ H = √((5k)² + (12k)²) = √(25k² + 144k²)

⇒ H = √(169k²) = 13k

⇒ sin θ = P / H = 5k / 13k = 5/13

This corresponds to **Option 2** as provided in the question.

**∴ The correct answer is 5/13.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

Common sets of integers (a, b, c) that satisfy a² + b² = c² include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

Trigonometric Ratios

For an acute angle: **sin θ** = Opp/Hyp, **cos θ** = Adj/Hyp, and **tan θ** = Opp/Adj.

questions.question: If each entry of a piece of data is increased by 7, then the arithmetic mean:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Let the original data be x₁ , x₂ , x₃ , . . . , xn.

**Formula Used:**

Arithmetic mean = (x₁ + x₂ + x₃ + . . . + xn) / n

**Calculation:**

⇒ If each entry is increased by 7, the new data becomes (x₁ + 7) , (x₂ + 7) , (x₃ + 7) , . . . , (xn + 7).

⇒ New arithmetic mean = [(x₁ + 7) + (x₂ + 7) + (x₃ + 7) + . . . + (xn + 7)] / n

⇒ New arithmetic mean = (x₁ + x₂ + x₃ + . . . + xn) / n + (7 + 7 + 7 + . . . + 7) / n

⇒ New arithmetic mean = Arithmetic mean + 7

**Therefore, the correct option is 1.**

questions.question: If the HCF of 85 and 153 is expressible in the form of 85x - 153, then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find the **HCF** of 85 and 153 by identifying their common factors:

85 = 5 × 17

153 = 9 × 17

Thus, **HCF** = 17.

Equate the given expression to the HCF: 85x − 153 = 17 ⇒ 85x = 170 ⇒ x = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 85 and 153.

The **HCF** of 85 and 153 is expressible in the form 85x − 153.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3bafa23b709d1d4067dfbadc7f69a109ee4805a8562a8ba31a56860951041b00.png] 

**Formula Used:**

The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** of two integers is the largest positive integer that divides both numbers without leaving a remainder.

**Calculations:**

Find the prime factorisation of both numbers:

⇒ 85 = 5 × 17

⇒ 153 = 3 × 3 × 17 = 3² × 17

Identify the common factor between 85 and 153:

⇒ Common Factor = 17

⇒ HCF(85, 153) = 17

According to the problem, the HCF is equal to 85x − 153:

⇒ 85x − 153 = 17

⇒ 85x = 17 + 153

⇒ 85x = 170

⇒ x = 170 ÷ 85

⇒ x = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The **HCF** of two or more numbers is the greatest common divisor that divides each of them exactly without leaving any remainder.

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two positive integers a and b, the product of their HCF and LCM is equal to the product of the numbers: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

Euclid's Division Algorithm

An efficient method to calculate the **HCF** of two integers by repeatedly expressing the larger number in terms of the smaller one using the division lemma (a = bq + r) until the remainder r becomes zero.</p

questions.question: If SA and SB are tangents to a circle from an outside point S, such that SA = 12 cm and angle ASB = 60°. What will the length of chord AB be?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Tangents drawn from an **external point** to a circle are always **equal** in length ⇒ **SA = SB = 12 cm**.

In triangle **SAB**, since **SA = SB** and the included angle **∠ASB = 60°**, the triangle must be **equilateral**.

For any equilateral triangle, all sides are equal ⇒ **AB = SA = SB = 12 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Tangent **SA = 12 cm** and **∠ASB = 60°**.

**Formula Used:** Length of tangents from an external point are equal; Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e47c59bfdbb9384c07708944203e293ccee291a852e3564b90905f5eb6ec7881.png] 

⇒ In Δ**SAB**, **SA = SB** (Length of tangents from external point **S** are equal).

⇒ Since **SA = SB**, then **∠SAB = ∠SBA** (Angles opposite to equal sides).

⇒ In Δ**SAB**, **∠ASB + ∠SAB + ∠SBA = 180°**.

⇒ **60° + 2 × ∠SAB = 180°**.

⇒ **2 × ∠SAB = 120°** ⇒ **∠SAB = 60°**.

⇒ Therefore, **∠SAB = ∠SBA = ∠ASB = 60°**.

⇒ This implies Δ**SAB** is an **equilateral triangle**.

⇒ **AB = SA = SB = 12 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent-Radius Property

The radius of a circle is always perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact (∠OAS = ∠OBS = 90°).

External Point Tangents

The lengths of the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal (SA = SB).

Line Joining Center and External Point

The line joining the center of the circle to the external point (SO) bisects the angle between the two tangents (∠ASO = ∠BSO).</p

(124 × 10) + (2 × 4) = 1240 + 8 = 1248

(1248 × 10) + (2 × 8) = 12480 + 16 = 12496

(12496 × 10) + (2 × 6) = 124960 + 12 = 124972

Hence, '124972' is the next term in the given series.
